title: Repair leaderboard tie rankings
instructions:
Fix two bugs in the existing `Leaderboard` implementation: names within tied
scores are sorted in the wrong direction, and tied players get different ranks.
Preserve the public API below.

## Files
- `leaderboard.py`

- `Leaderboard()` starts empty.
- `set_score(name: str, score: int) -> None` adds or replaces a player's score.
  Names are nonempty strings and scores are integers; assume valid input.
- `remove(name: str) -> bool` returns `True` when a player was removed and `False`
  when absent.
- `ranking() -> list[tuple[int, str, int]]` returns fresh `(rank, name, score)`
  triples sorted by decreasing score, then increasing name using Python's normal
  case-sensitive string order. Use competition ranks: scores `9, 9, 5` have
  ranks `1, 1, 3`. Multiple groups of ties each skip the occupied positions.
  Negative scores and zero work the same way. An empty board returns `[]`.
- `top(count: int) -> list[tuple[int, str, int]]` returns at most `count` entries
  from `ranking()`, even if the cutoff splits a tie. Zero returns `[]`; negative
  values raise `ValueError`. Assume an integer count.
- `rank_of(name: str) -> int | None` returns the current rank, or `None` if absent.
Updates and removals must be reflected by all queries. Editing a returned list
must not change the board.
